name: Citation Management Common Pitfalls
description: This module lists frequently observed mistakes, bugs, and anti-patterns seen in everyday citation management work, so they can be recognized and avoided during typical citation management tasks.
content:
This module lists frequently observed mistakes, bugs, and anti-patterns seen in everyday citation management work, so they can be recognized and avoided during typical citation management tasks.

CORE GUIDELINES
1. When citation management decisions are ambiguous, favor the option that is easiest to reverse or extend later.
2. Keep citation management outputs reproducible: fix seeds, record versions, and avoid hidden non-determinism where it matters.
3. State assumptions about citation management explicitly before proceeding, rather than leaving them implicit.
4. Document any non-obvious citation management decision with a short rationale so future readers understand the 'why', not just the 'what'.
5. Measure before optimizing any citation management bottleneck; do not guess at what is slow.
6. When multiple citation management strategies are viable, name the trade-off explicitly rather than silently picking one.
7. When citation management guidance conflicts with a specific user instruction, defer to the user's explicit instruction and note the conflict.

COMMON PITFALLS TO AVOID
- Do not apply generic citation management advice without checking it fits the specific context at hand.
- Do not silently drop citation management edge cases to make an example look cleaner than the real system.
- Do not skip documenting citation management assumptions just because they seem obvious in the moment.

CLOSING NOTE
These guidelines are a starting point for citation management, not an exhaustive rulebook — use judgment when a rule doesn't fit the situation.
